question: If a constant force (F) of 20 N moves an object through a displacement (d) of 5 m in the same direction, then what will be the work (W) done?
solution:
The correct answer is __**100 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work done (W)** is defined as the product of the **magnitude of the force** applied and the **displacement** of the object in the direction of that force.
 
• The mathematical formula for work is **W = F × d × cos(θ)**, where **F** represents the **constant force**, **d** is the **displacement**, and **θ** is the **angle** between the force and the direction of motion.
 
• In this specific case, the **constant force (F)** is given as **20 N** and the **displacement (d)** is **5 m**.
 
• Since the object moves in the **same direction** as the force, the **angle (θ)** is **0 degrees**. The value of **cos(0°)** is **1**.
 
• Substituting the values into the formula: **W = 20 N × 5 m × 1 = 100 J**. Thus, the work done is **100 Joules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Work**: **Work** is a **scalar quantity**, which means it has only **magnitude** and no **direction**, even though it is derived from two **vector quantities** (force and displacement).
 
• **SI Unit**: The **Standard International (SI) unit** of work is the **Joule (J)**. One Joule is defined as the work performed when a force of **1 Newton (N)** displaces an object by **1 meter (m)**.
 
• **Positive, Negative, and Zero Work**:
 
 
• **Positive Work** occurs when the force and displacement are in the **same direction** (0° ≤ θ 
 
 
• **Relationship with Energy**: Work is closely related to **energy**. When work is done on an object, **energy is transferred** to that object. For example, lifting an object involves doing work against **gravity**, which increases the object's **potential energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dimensional Formula**: The **dimensional formula** for work is **[ML²T⁻²]**. This is identical to the dimensions of **kinetic energy** and **potential energy**, confirming the **Work-Energy Theorem**.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: This theorem states that the **net work done** by all forces acting on a body is equal to the **change in its kinetic energy**.
 
• **CGS Unit**: In the **Centimetre-Gram-Second (CGS) system**, the unit of work is the **erg**. One **Joule** is equal to **10,000,000 (10⁷) ergs**.
 
• **Power and Work**: **Power** is defined as the **rate of doing work**. It is calculated by dividing the **work done** by the **time (t)** taken to complete it (**P = W / t**). The SI unit for power is the **Watt (W)**.
